A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ComFe, with matching architecture, benchmarks, and substantial retained results. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original ComFe classification, robustness, OOD-detection, ablation, and qualitative visualization results in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: V3 retains original ComFe experiments and reports additional sensitivity studies, class-prototype visualizations, and image-manipulation results.

M1.justification: Explanation retrieval changes from direct nearest training image prototypes in v1 Figure 5 to exemplars of a selected class prototype in v3 Figure 3 and Section 4.3. The backbone, decoder, and principal loss components remain; moving the prototype-level discriminative term into the auxiliary loss does not introduce a new component.

E1.justification: The classification and OOD datasets remain the same. V3 Figure S6 adds an Oxford Pets test scenario with informative or other image regions removed, extending evaluation to deliberately altered inputs.

E2.justification: The interpretable and linear baselines in Tables 1–3 and the KNN+, Energy, and NN-Guide OOD comparators are retained. V3 Table S4 explicitly displays a linear baseline already involved in v1 Section 5's background-prototype comparison. Removing INTR from Table 2's caption does not remove an evaluated row.

E3.justification: Default training budgets, architecture settings, datasets, and metrics remain unchanged. V3 adds targeted temperature, smoothing, and prototype-count sweep protocols and image-region removal tests. The background-prototype ablation changes from ViT-L in v1 Table 4 to ViT-S in v3 Table S4, preventing a same-setting comparison of those results.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends the existing depth and loss ablations with temperature, label-smoothing, and prototype-count sensitivity studies, class-prototype utilization analysis, and image-manipulation faithfulness cases. It also replaces the large-backbone background ablation with a small-backbone experiment. OOD, register, reliability, and initialization analyses largely match retained material.

E5.justification: V1 explicitly reports five-run means and standard deviations for decoder-depth ablations and shows uncertainty for loss ablations without specifying their run count. V3 explicitly applies five runs and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting to all ablations. This clarifies reporting; it does not establish an increase in runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Depth and loss ablation values change: two-layer Aircraft accuracy, for example, changes from 76.0±0.8 in v1 Table S4 to 77.2±0.9 in v3 Table S8. V3 adds sensitivity and qualitative results and replaces ViT-L no-background results with ViT-S results. Main Tables 1–3, OOD scores, and register scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 substantially reworks v1's image-level mixture formulation into an explicit patch-prototype-class joint model, states conditional independence and a uniform image-prototype prior, and develops the image-label likelihood in Section 3 and Appendix A. It also changes the patch-posterior temperature from tau_2 in v1 Equation 15 to tau_1 in v3 Equation 8. These exceed relocation or notation changes.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain an interpretable foundation-model classifier using component features, scalability to ImageNet, competitive or superior classification performance, shared hyperparameters across datasets, and improved robustness relative to a linear head. The rewritten abstract, consolidated contribution list, and new conclusion retain these claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of unused class prototypes and masking faithfulness, and moderates the earlier conclusions about decoder depth and auxiliary-loss benefits. Its background-prototype discussion emphasizes benefits on ViT-S while dropping v1's contrary ViT-L finding. Initialization sensitivity and backbone context leakage remain documented.

D1.justification: V3 adds training pseudocode, identifies the default label-smoothing value in Table S11, and provides further augmentation details. Section 4.1 changes a promised future GitHub release into a statement that code is available. Hardware, training-time estimates, and principal implementation settings remain unchanged; actual repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to the original Vision Transformer paper and DINO as a von Mises-Fisher mixture model. It expands comparisons with ProtoP approaches, particularly their final classification layer and background-prototype issues. The principal related-work families and positioning relative to INTR remain.

P1.justification: V3 changes the title and extensively rewrites the abstract, motivation, and methodological narrative. It integrates much of the former discussion into the results, adds a conclusion, and reorganizes the supplement into derivation, class-prototype visualization, additional results, and ablation sections.

P2.justification: V3 changes the document template and extensively rearranges displays. It redraws Figure 1, replaces the nearest-neighbor explanation display with class-prototype exemplars, adds prototype grids, masking examples, and sensitivity tables, and relocates existing seed and robustness figures. V1's introductory fish-clustering illustration is removed.

improvement.justification: V3 better supports its interpretability and hyperparameter-insensitivity claims through class-prototype exemplars, masking cases, and additional controlled sweeps; pseudocode also improves documentation. These extend an already substantial evaluation in v1. Removing the ViT-L no-background results weakens qualification of the background-prototype claim, limiting the net improvement.
